questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had written a very long report, but this website kicked me out and now everything is gone, and there is no way I am spending another hour on this survey, therefore this will mostly be written in keywords. 

To make it perfectly clear I would not recommend anyone to go to this university. I had a good time, but that was despite this university and not because of the university. Luckily I got what I came for; language skills and a resumé boost, which I think landed me the dream job.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Ridiculing that UCPH has this university marked as a 'good place' for a Statskundskaber to go on an exchange stay. Impossible for a bachelor student to get the necessary courses approved, thus I had to use the BAKA-arrangement (which is an arrangement that lets you take master courses while being on the bachelor) to even be able to go.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Info on the introduction day on the university, nothing upon arrival

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I guess it was possible to contact the student administration? I'm not sure what is meant by assistance, but you received a welcome letter and a time, date, and address for the introduction day.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I don't know, as I just told you I found housing through my host institution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you should get a metro card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The university helped me find housing through the French Crous-system. It was pretty cheap, but I was allocated a studio that might as well could have been located in North Africa. Poverty and many homeless people, girls advised to not go home alone in the evening, just a weird vibe in that area of town and definitely not a Paris-feel. Nordvest on crack is probably a good description. 
On the plus side though; it was near a metro line and the Parisian metro system is wonderful.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The French bureaucratic system will suck the life out of you

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was done online

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contacting the student administration

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Comically bad course selection for a political science student

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Investigate the course selection very thoroughly before applying. I did look at the course selection before applying, but apparently many of the courses are only offered in one of the two semesters, effectually cutting the course selection in half.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned this shouldn't be an institution that UCPH, or at least Statskundskab, promotes

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very fluctuating I had 6 ECTS point courses that were like high-school easy and then I had 3 ECTS point courses where I'm not even sure I'm going to pass

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More high-school like. I like the UCPH style of a lecture and then a debate-style smaller classroom thing. Also, French professors will for some reason talk a lot of French in class to the French students even though it is an English course. Pretty frustrating.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Intermediate Microeconomics, International Finance, GoTo Market Strategies, Strategic Management, Current Research in Sociological Economics, International Politics, Management of Information Systems and Gender Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Politics were really interesting, expect a lot of reading and a very demeaning and patronizing teacher, but also pretty much the only politics related course available.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The fee of getting the housing assistance from Dauphine was like 1000.- DKK

Dauphine also provided an intensive language course in the first week which was about 1500.- DKK. The course was online the first two days, and I didn't receive a link in time, so I missed the first 1,5 days. The last three days of the language course was overlapping with other courses and the introduction day, which made it impossible to participate. I asked the university for a refund, but 'sorry, that is not possible'. Basically, they stole 1500.- DKK from me

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Paris is very Copenhagenly priced.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great there were a lot of possibilities, but you also have to be quick due to the limited spots in all of the activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Debate club, trips around Paris, Sports clubs etc., there is a rich opportunity to engage with other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There will be a lot of parties, a lot of cultural things and events. If you, despite my very intense advice not to, go to this University get the best out of it and experience all the amazing things Paris has to offer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a weekend trip to Bretagne

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The French are actually very polite. You'll hear pardons everywhere. But a lot of them don't speak any English, so at least learn a little bit of the French glossary if you choose to go to France.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think it's very common to fall into the exchange-student trap, most people I know mostly socialized with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Learning French

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very Parisian way of life; cafées, restaurants, boulangeries, the overall culture and feel of Paris is great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a chaotic experience. Use the stay to your advantage (learn the language and make it a boost for your resumé). Lastly don't go here if I haven't already made myself perfectly clear.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to live in another country is really an interesting and developing experience

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to solve every problem that arises in a country where you know no one, and trust me there will come a lot of problems.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Luckily I got to go and the fairy tale had a happy ending, but I honestly feel mocked by UCPH with the fact that they promoted Dauphine as a good place to go on exchange for a PolSci student.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
